'''Mellen Woodman Haskell''' (March 17, 1863 – January 15, 1948) was an American [[mathematician]], specializing in [[geometry]], [[group theory]], and applications of group theory to geometry.

==Education and career==
After secondary education at [[Roxbury Latin School]], he received in 1883 his bachelor's degree and in 1885 his [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] and a Parker Traveling Fellowship from [[Harvard University]]. From 1885 to 1889 he studied mathematics at the [[University of Leipzig]] and the [[University of Göttingen]], where in 1889 he received, under [[Felix Klein]], his [[Dr. phil.]]<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uMvcfEYr6tsC&pg=PA209|author=Parshall, Karen|authorlink=Karen Parshall|author2=Rowe, David E.|authorlink2=David E. Rowe|title=The Emergence of the American Mathematical Research Community 1876–1900: J. J. Sylvester, Felix Klein, and E. H. Moore|series=AMS/LMS History of Mathematics 8|location= Providence/London|year=1994|pages=209–210|isbn=9780821809075}}</ref> In 1889 Haskell became an instructor at the [[University of Michigan]].

In 1890 he was hired by the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as an assistant professor. He was promoted to associate professor in 1894, and in 1906 to [[professor]]. In 1909 he became the chair of U. C. Berkeley's mathematics department in succession to [[Irving Stringham]], and remained the chair until retiring as professor emeritus in 1933.<ref name=UCBerkeleyObit>W. M. Hart, C. A. Noble & [[Griffith C. Evans]] (1948) {{cite web|url=http://texts.cdlib.org/view?docId=hb9p300969&doc.view=frames&chunk.id=div00014&toc.depth=1&toc.id=|title= Mellen Woodman Haskell, University of California: In Memoriam}}, via [[Online Archive of California]]</ref>

Haskell provided a foundation for [[hyperbolic angle]] and [[hyperbolic functions]] with his article in ''Bulletin of American Mathematical Society'' in 1895. In particular, he identified the angle with [[area]] of a [[hyperbolic sector]], and showed its invariance under [[squeeze mapping]].

Haskell was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1924 in [[Toronto]] and in 1928 in [[Bologna]].

==Personal life==
Haskell married Isabel Woodford Brown in 1928.<ref name=Noted>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-berkeley-gazette-noted-campus-leader/173517388/ |title=Noted Campus Leader Dies |newspaper=[[Berkeley Gazette]] |page=1 |date=1948-01-16 |access-date=2025-05-31 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

He died in Berkeley on January 15, 1948.<ref name=Noted/>

==Selected publications==
* 1890: "Ueber die zu der Curve λ<sup>3</sup>μ+ μ<sup>3</sup>ν+ μ<sup>3</sup>λ= 0 im projectiven Sinne gehörende mehrfache Ueberdeckung der Ebene", [[American Journal of Mathematics]] : 1–52. {{doi|10.2307/2369597}}
* 1892: "Note on resultants", [[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] 1: 223–224. {{MR|1557188}}
* 1893: "On the definition of logarithms", ''Bulletin of the  American Mathematical Society'' 2: 164–167. {{MR|1557235}} 
* 1895: [http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183414352 On the introduction of the notion of hyperbolic functions], ''Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society'' 1: 155–159, from [[Project Euclid]] {{MR|1557371}}
* 1903: [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=umn.319510002320924;view=1up;seq=11 "On a Certain Rational Cubic Transformation in Space"], [[The American Mathematical Monthly]] 10(1): 1–3.
* 1903; [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=umn.319510002320924;view=1up;seq=40 "Generalization of a Fundamental Theorem in the Geometry of the Triangle"], ''The American Mathematical Monthly'' 10(2): 30–33.
* 1905: "The construction of conics under given conditions", ''Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society'' 11: 268–273. {{MR|1558211}}
* 1906: "The resolution of any collineation into perspective reflections", [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] 7: 361–369. {{MR|1500754}}
* 1917: "The maximum number of cusps of an algebraic plane curve, and enumeration of self-dual curves", ''[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]'' 23: 164–165. {{MR|1559901}}

===As translator===
* 1893: [[Felix Klein]], "[http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183407629 A comparative review of recent researches in geometry]", ''Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society'' 2: 215–249, from Project Euclid {{MR|1557253}} (See also [[Erlangen program]].)
